entry: American singer-songwriter. Her self-titled debut album, released in 1988 by Elektra Records, became a commercial success after her appearance at the [[Nelson Mandela]] 70th Birthday Tribute concert and was certified 6× platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America. It earned three Grammy Awards, including Best New Artist. In 2023, after Luke Combs covered her song "Fast Car," Chapman became the first Black person to score a country number one with a solo composition.

East-to-west prevailing winds in Earth's equatorial region, blowing mainly from the northeast in the Northern Hemisphere and from the southeast in the Southern Hemisphere. They strengthen in winter and form part of the [[Hadley cell]], in which surface air flows toward the equator. Captains of sailing ships have used them to cross the world's oceans for centuries, enabling European colonization of the Americas. In meteorology, they steer tropical storms over the Atlantic, Pacific, and southern Indian oceans, which cause rainfall in East Africa, Madagascar, North America, and [[Southeast Asia]]. Trade winds also carry nitrate- and phosphate-rich [[Sahara|Saharan]] dust to [[Latin America]] and the Caribbean Sea.

Alternative medical practice drawn from [[Traditional medicine|traditional medicine]] in China. Most of its claims are pseudoscientific, and most treatments lack robust evidence of effectiveness or a logical mechanism of action. Some ingredients are toxic and can cause disease, including cancer. Its modern form is largely a 20th-century invention: early 20th-century modernizers tried to eliminate traditional practices, and practitioners then organized selected elements of philosophy and practice as "Chinese medicine." During the [[Cultural Revolution]] of the 1960s, the government promoted it as inexpensive and popular, a policy largely spearheaded by [[Mao Zedong]], who according to one account did not believe in its effectiveness. Its core concept, that [[Qi|qi]] circulates through meridians linked to organs, has no supporting evidence: there is no evidence that meridians or vital energy exist. The demand for traditional medicines in China is a major driver of illegal wildlife smuggling.

Animation technique in which each frame is drawn by hand, also called classical, cel, or hand-drawn animation. It was the dominant form of animation in the United States through the 20th century, until the industry shifted to [[Computer animation|computer animation]]. Production usually begins with a script and a storyboard, and dialogue is recorded before animation so that character movement can be synchronized to the soundtrack. A timing director prepares an exposure sheet (X-sheet) that breaks down the action, dialogue, and sound frame by frame for the animators. Layout artists then set camera angles, paths, lighting, and shading. Today the process survives mainly as digital ink and paint, which combines hand-drawn elements with computer compositing.

Knowledge, skills, and practices rooted in the cultural beliefs of various societies, used to treat illness and maintain health, especially among Indigenous groups. Systems include [[Ayurveda]], [[Traditional Chinese medicine|traditional Chinese medicine]], and Unani. A 2024 [[World Health Organization|WHO]] global survey found that two-thirds of countries report at least 40% of their population uses traditional, complementary, or integrative medicine. Use of medicinal herbs spans over 5,000 years, from the Sumerians and Egyptians through Greek, Roman, Islamic, and medieval European traditions. Critics point to the lack of scientific evidence and to the use of endangered animals such as slow lorises, sharks, elephants, and pangolins, which contributes to biodiversity loss and illegal wildlife trade. The WHO supports integration of these practices but calls for more research on their safety and effectiveness.

Incident in which a vehicle collides with another vehicle, a pedestrian, an animal, road debris, or a stationary obstruction. Also called a car crash, a collision often causes injury, disability, death, and property damage. Road transport is statistically the most dangerous daily situation people face, though its casualties attract less media attention than rarer tragedies. In 2013, 54 million people worldwide were injured and 1.4 million died, up from 1.1 million deaths in 1990. Middle-income countries have the highest death rate, at 20 deaths per 100,000 inhabitants. Risk factors include speed, road design, weather, [[Driving under the influence|impairment by alcohol or drugs]], and aggressive or distracted driving. The [[Associated Press]] now recommends "crash" or "collision" over "accident" unless culpability is proven.

Movement of vehicles and pedestrians along land routes. Organized traffic has established priorities, lanes, right-of-way rules, and traffic control at intersections, which generally improves both safety and efficiency. Traffic is often classified as heavy motor vehicles, such as cars and trucks, other vehicles such as mopeds and bicycles, and pedestrians. The basic rules of the road are set by the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic, an international treaty under the authority of the [[United Nations]], although not all countries are signatories. Road construction, collisions, and debris disrupt flow; on busy freeways a minor disruption can persist as a traffic wave, and a complete breakdown may cause congestion and gridlock. Simulations of traffic apply [[Stochastic process|stochastic processes]], queuing theory, and equations of mathematical physics.

Genre of drama based on human suffering, in which terrible or sorrowful events befall a main character or cast. Traditionally, tragedy aims to produce catharsis, a "pain [that] awakens pleasure," in its audience. The form originated in [[Ancient Greece|ancient Greece]] about 2,500 years ago, where [[Aeschylus]], [[Sophocles]], and [[Euripides]] wrote the best-known surviving works. In his *Poetics* (335 BCE), [[Aristotle]] distinguished tragedy from comedy and epic poetry. Later playwrights extended the form: Shakespeare's *Hamlet* and *King Lear* blend fate with human choice, and [[Henrik Ibsen]]'s naturalistic tragedy shaped the modern stage. Modern dramatists such as [[Samuel Beckett]] and [[Arthur Miller]] applied the form to despair and to the common man.

Dilemma in which individuals overuse a shared resource, depleting it for everyone. The term is the title of a 1968 essay by ecologist Garrett Hardin, published in [[Science (journal)|Science]], though the idea goes back to [[Aristotle]]. Hardin's main concern was overpopulation, and he argued that the right to choose family size should be replaced by "mutual coercion, mutually agreed upon." His views on population have been criticized as simplistic, eugenicist, and racist. Elinor Ostrom, who won the Nobel Prize in Economics, is seen by some economists as having refuted Hardin's claims.

Dirt or small paved road, usually through an undeveloped natural area, designed mainly for pedestrians, equestrians, and non-motorized vehicles. Some trails are restricted to walkers, cyclists, or equestrians, while others are shared-use, and most ban motorized vehicles, although some unpaved trails allow dirt bikes and other off-road vehicles. In the United States, the term historically described westward expansion routes such as the [[Oregon Trail]]. Usage varies: in the [[United Kingdom]], footpath is preferred for pedestrian routes, while in [[Australia]] track is used interchangeably with trail. Animals created the first trails, which humans later adapted, and farmers moved cattle along drove roads. Former railway rights of way and canal towpaths have become recreational trails, and ancient routes such as the [[Silk Road]] covered great distances.

Forced displacement of about 60,000 Native Americans of the "Five Civilized Tribes" by the U.S. government between 1830 and 1850. After President [[Andrew Jackson]] won passage of the Indian Removal Act of 1830, the Cherokee, Muscogee, Seminole, Chickasaw, and Choctaw nations were moved from the Southeast to Indian Territory west of the [[Mississippi River]]. The Cherokee removal of 1838, the last forced removal east of the Mississippi, followed the 1828 discovery of gold near Dahlonega, [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]]. Disease, exposure, and starvation killed thousands. Some scholars classify the events as [[Genocide|genocide]]; others call them ethnic cleansing.

Railway facility where trains stop to load or unload passengers, freight, or both. It usually has at least one platform and a station building offering ticket sales, waiting rooms, and baggage or freight service. Stations on single-track lines often have a passing loop. Many stations date from the 19th century and reflect its grandiose architecture. In the United States, "depot" is an alternative name used for both passenger and freight facilities. The world's first recorded railway station, serving horse-drawn trains, opened in [[Swansea]], Wales, in 1807. The oldest terminal station in the world, Crown Street station in [[Liverpool]], England, was built in 1830 on the locomotive-hauled line to [[Manchester]].

1996 British black comedy-drama film directed by [[Danny Boyle]]. Adapted from Irvine Welsh's 1993 novel, *Trainspotting* follows a group of [[Heroin|heroin]] addicts in an economically depressed area of [[Edinburgh]], centered on Mark Renton, played by [[Ewan McGregor]]. It was released in the United Kingdom on February 23, 1996, and many critics regard it as one of the best films of the 1990s. The British Film Institute ranked it tenth in its list of Top 100 British films of the 20th century. A sequel, *T2 Trainspotting*, was released in January 2017.

Roman emperor (r. AD 98–117). Born in Italica in Hispania Baetica, present-day [[Spain]], Trajan was the first emperor born outside Italy and the second of the Five Good Emperors of the [[Nerva–Antonine dynasty]]. He rose under [[Domitian]], was adopted as heir by the elderly Nerva, and was given the title *optimus princeps* ("the best ruler") by the Senate. He annexed Dacia and Nabataea, and his war with the [[Parthian Empire]] added Armenia, Mesopotamia, and Assyria as provinces, though these gains were largely reversed after his death. By the time of his death the Roman Empire had reached its maximum territorial extent. He died of a stroke while sailing back to Rome and was deified by the Senate and by his successor, [[Hadrian]].

Form of urban rail transit whose vehicles run on tracks laid on or beside public streets, also called a streetcar or trolley. Trams are a type of light rail and generally the smallest-scale form of rail transit. They operate in mixed traffic, and their larger size and steel wheels give them greater capacity and energy efficiency than [[Bus|buses]]. Most use electric power from an overhead line through a pantograph. Electric trams largely replaced horse-drawn cars in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, declined as buses improved, and have seen a resurgence since the 1980s. The English word derives from a Scots term for a coal-mine truck.

Minor planet orbiting the [[Sun]] at a greater average distance than [[Neptune]]. Its main groups are the classical and resonant objects of the [[Kuiper belt]], the scattered disc, and the distant sednoids. The first, Pluto, was discovered in 1930; the second, 15760 Albion, not until 1992. [[Eris (dwarf planet)|Eris]] is the most massive known, followed by Pluto, [[Haumea]], [[Makemake]], and [[Gonggong (dwarf planet)|Gonggong]]. More than 80 satellites have been found in orbit around these bodies, which are thought to be mixtures of rock, amorphous carbon, and volatile ices such as water and methane.

Extensive family of Papuan languages spoken on [[New Guinea]] and neighboring islands, mainly in [[Papua New Guinea]] and Indonesia. It is perhaps the third-largest [[Language family|language family]] by number of languages, spoken by around 3 million people. Its core is considered established, but its boundaries and membership remain uncertain. In 1975 Stephen Wurm expanded the proposed family to over 500 languages spoken by some 2,300,000 people, though much of his evidence was typological. In 2005 Malcolm Ross proposed a reduced version based solely on lexical resemblances. Other linguists, such as William A. Foley, rejected much of the grouping and broke it into smaller families and isolates.

Trade between North Africa and the rest of Africa, conducted by camel caravans across the [[Sahara]]. Its peak ran from the 8th century until the early 17th century. The desert once separated the Mediterranean economy from the [[Niger River]] basin, and crossing it paid only when exceptional circumstances outweighed the cost and danger. Some caravans were as large as 12,000 camels, according to [[Ibn Battuta]], and they were guided by highly paid [[Berbers]] who knew the desert. Gold was bartered for salt, and goods also included ivory and kola nuts. Many West African states adopted Arabic writing and the religion of North Africa. The trade also included enslaved people, with estimates of the total running into the millions.

Railway linking European Russia with the Russian Far East, the longest railway line in the world. It spans 9,289 km (5,772 mi) from [[Moscow]] to [[Vladivostok]], crossing a record eight time zones. Government ministers personally appointed by Alexander III and [[Nicholas II]] supervised its construction between 1891 and 1916. Since 1916 it has directly connected Moscow with Vladivostok. Branch routes run through [[Manchuria]] to [[Beijing]] and through [[Ulaanbaatar]] in Mongolia, while the Baikal–Amur Mainline, completed in 1991, follows a more northerly course past [[Lake Baikal]]. The full journey once took eight days. Today the fully electrified, predominantly double-tracked line carries passenger trains and substantial freight.

Woman assigned male at birth, also called a [[Transgender|transgender]] woman. Many trans women experience gender dysphoria, the distress that can arise from incongruence between gender identity and physical sex characteristics, and gender transition can reduce it. Social transition often includes a new name, hairstyle, clothing, and voice, while feminizing hormone therapy develops breasts. Trans women may have any sexual or romantic orientation. In the [[United States]], discrimination is particularly severe against non-white trans women, who face the intersection of transphobia, [[Misogyny|misogyny]], and [[Racism|racism]] and are at heightened risk of violence and hate crimes.

Mountain range of uplifted, mostly sedimentary rock crossing [[Antarctica]]. About 3,500 km (2,000 mi) long, it divides East and West Antarctica and is one of the longest mountain ranges on Earth. Its highest peak, Mount Kirkpatrick, rises 4,528 m (14,856 ft). The range was uplifted beginning about 65 million years ago during the opening of the West Antarctic Rift System. Its sedimentary layers, including Beacon Supergroup sandstones and coal, rest on granites and gneisses. The McMurdo Dry Valleys, the largest stretch of Antarctic snow and ice-free terrain, lie within the range. Forests once covered the continent, and the last trees are believed to have grown here before cooling linked to the breakup of [[Gondwana]] eliminated them. The range was first crossed during the British National Antarctic Expedition of 1901–1904.

Philosophical, spiritual, and literary movement that developed in [[New England]] in the late 1820s and 1830s. Its core belief is in the inherent goodness of people and nature, and people are at their best when self-reliant. It emphasized intuition over empiricism and developed alongside [[Unitarianism]] at [[Harvard University]], drawing on [[Romanticism]] and the philosophy of [[Immanuel Kant|Kant]]. Members of the Transcendental Club, founded in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]] in 1836, included [[Ralph Waldo Emerson]] and [[Henry David Thoreau]]. Thoreau's *Walden* (1854) is a central text.

Process of duplicating a segment of [[DNA]] into [[RNA]] for [[Gene expression|gene expression]]. RNA polymerase reads one DNA strand and produces a complementary RNA strand, called a primary transcript. Some transcripts are messenger RNA (mRNA), which encodes [[Protein|proteins]], while others are non-coding RNAs. The RNA uses uracil wherever DNA uses thymine. Transcription proceeds through initiation, promoter escape, elongation, and termination. Enhancers, which can lie far from a gene's start site, can increase its transcription up to 100-fold. In [[Virus|virology]], the term refers to mRNA synthesis from a viral RNA molecule. Regulation through transcription factors and enhancers determines when and how much RNA is produced.

Passive electrical component that transfers energy between circuits through [[Electromagnetic induction|electromagnetic induction]]. A varying current in one coil produces a varying magnetic flux in the core, which induces a voltage across the other coils. [[Faraday's law of induction]], discovered in 1831, describes this effect. The voltage ratio equals the turns ratio between windings, so transformers step voltage up or down, and they can also provide galvanic isolation between circuits. Since the first constant-potential transformer in 1885, they have been essential to transmitting and distributing [[Alternating current|alternating current]] power. Their size ranges from RF units smaller than a cubic centimeter to units weighing hundreds of tons on the power grid. Real units lose energy through hysteresis and [[Eddy current|eddy current]] losses in the core and resistance in the windings.

Japanese–American mecha media franchise produced by Hasbro and Takara Tomy. It follows the heroic Autobots, led by Optimus Prime, and the villainous Decepticons, led by Megatron, two factions of alien robots that transform into vehicles and animals. The franchise spans toys, animation, comic books, video games, and films. As of 2011 it had generated more than ¥2 trillion ($25 billion) in revenue. *Dark of the Moon* (2011) and *Age of Extinction* (2014) each grossed more than $1 billion. Ownership is split between Hasbro, outside Japan, and Tomy, within Japan.
